items.text: Metropolis
Victor's Workshop, 1908

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Victor, how much gasoline is left?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Enough for a few tests, but we'll run out by next weekend.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Don't worry. Our investors will send us another barrel before that. Still, we'd best use it sparingly. This stuff is expensive.
The engineer turns the page on his calendar, staining it with oil.
Several drafts are pinned to the wall, each marked with notes and proposed changes.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: This pipe will not be enough. It may warp if the temperature is not controlled.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: There is no guarantee of stable heat transfer. Perhaps we should add an outer casing to improve its strength.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: What do you think, Victor?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Oh, now you're interested in my input? Sure, you don't want to ask someone else—maybe one of your nut-job colleagues?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The LSCC does not have any staff to spare for this project. I am afraid you will have to do it.
It has been six months since she heard about the engineer's project—the development of a true powered wingsuit—and dropped everything to join it.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: This fuel tank will be too small for a flight of any significant duration.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Not that it matters. Our engine is already severely limited by our materials and weight requirements.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But we can still give it a try. Our current improvements should meaningfully increase our flight time.
The mechanical woman turns to the wall and unpins several unneeded drafts.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Meaningful? I doubt we'll manage more than a few extra seconds.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: They're expecting results. Real results. They aren't going to pay for a few seconds.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: If the company pulls out, we'll have to terminate the project.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: And they've been delaying pay day a little more each month. Think they're trying to tell us something?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We have made progress. Our situation is not as grim as you make it out to be.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Are you going to give up?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Give up? No way!

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Do you know how much I've spent on this project already? Now, if I were smart, I would've never taken up this crazy scheme in the first place.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: There have been attempts before, Victor.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Yeah, I know. I remember the stories from when I was a kid. Granny flew like a bird over from Europe. Well, maybe she did figure it out, but she didn't think to write it down before she croaked.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: And there have been plenty of others that have tried since! Did even one of them succeed? No! Not a single goddamn one!

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: So, here I am, about to be the latest one to make the same damn fool mistakes. Maybe the last.
A moment of bitter clarity strikes the engineer.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The last one? Of course not.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Why would you think that? The dream of flight—no, I cannot imagine humanity ever giving up on it.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Are you aware this pointless debate has cumulatively wasted 3 hours 48 minutes and 19 seconds of our time—just this month?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Time you might have spent better on checking these wings.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Don't tell me what to do, Iron Head.
The engineer walks away, muttering unclear but targeted complaints, until he pivots and returns back to the wings.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Returning to my original query. I am concerned that heat from the exhaust will compromise the integrity of this piping.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Why not cool it down with water or something?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: A rapid shift in temperature would cause the pipe to explode.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I admit that it is unlikely that this would occur during the course of our current maximum flight time.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: However, I suggest a change of material to avoid potential issues as we extend its duration.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: That's not an option. We've only got what we've got.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Why? We could greatly increase our efficiency, not to mention safety.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Because our investors asked us to! They want a model for mass production.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Our top priority is to give them confidence, otherwise they will cut our funding.
"Cut our funding"—a threat that's looming ever nearer.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Do you know how long those Wright boys are keeping their contraption in the air now? We're losing our only opportunity to make something of this project.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The only opportunity?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: That is not true, Victor.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Even if they were three to five years ahead of us, it would make no difference. We are heirs to the work of centuries.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Besides, we are not precisely direct competitors.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: They have produced a rigid-wing aircraft, not a single-person wingsuit. There is room for both concepts.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Centuries?! Three to five years ahead of us?! How many three to five years are there before I'm dead and gone?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: You're wrong, Luce. If they bring that thing of theirs to the market first, they win. In this business, winner takes all, pal! And loser gets nothing, literally nothing!

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Even if we are not commercially successful, our work will not be meaningless, as long as we advance scientific knowledge.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Yeah, maybe that's enough for your egghead pals at LSCC! But there's no glory in second place, Luce. No fame. No money. Not a red cent!
He seizes up, as if his rage is bubbling up under his skin, ready to explode.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Calm yourself, Victor.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Go get the car. We will have a test flight at the parking lot in two hours.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Didn't I already tell you not to bark orders at me?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Sorry, Ms. Lucy. I'm just frustrated. I'm on a short fuse these days.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We should focus on our work, Victor.
The telephone rings.
Victor runs toward the phone, slipping over the slick oil. He's half-cursing as he picks up the receiver.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Dammit—yes, hi, hello, yeah, this is Victor speaking. How can I—

items.speaker: Investor
items.text: Mr. Victor, we deeply regret that we must speak to you, due to some recent developments with our competitors.

items.speaker: Investor
items.text: We've been forced to reassess your project, and we've come to the conclusion that it is no-longer economical for us to maintain our involvement.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: "Economical"? What do you mean?

items.speaker: Investor
items.text: Simply put, we will be no longer providing any further funding or material support.

items.speaker: Investor
items.text: Given the growing success of your competitors and your own lack of results, it appears there is no longer a viable future for this project.

items.speaker: Investor
items.text: We appreciate your understanding in all of this. You will be hearing from us if we require your services in the future.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Hey! Don't hang up! What the hell are you saying?!

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Hey! Hey!

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Bastards.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: What is happening?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Got good news, and bad. Which one do you want to hear first?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You look pale. Tell me the good news first.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: The good news is we don't have to listen to those ignoramuses we called investors anymore.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: The bad news is they're out.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I see. So, they have abandoned the project?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: In a manner of speaking.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But we have not abandoned it.
The engineer sits down on the oily stool, head in palms, inadvertently smearing oil over his hair.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: I've got some friends to call. They might be able to salvage this mess.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: In the meantime, perhaps we should take a break. Would you like some coffee?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: What? Coffee, nah ... thanks, Luce. But I'm not taking a break, this is it. It's over.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Oh?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: It was a fool's dream, Luce. Leave the flying to the birds and those damned Wright Brothers.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: I'm talking about selling off all this junk. We might cover a part of our losses still.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Are you that easily defeated?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We still have sufficient materials to improve on our current design.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Oh, sure, and what about the one after that? Experiment after experiment, how many more times do I gotta fail before I wise up?

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: And what's the use? Even if we could do it, we're already too late.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Come on, go get the car. We can run the experiment on the beach.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: No, actually, we should go to the Charles River.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: What are you up to?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The wind coming off the river will be steadier.
He moves to get up, but sinks down. Unsure of his next move, looking like a ship tossing in a storm.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: One last run then? For old time's sakes?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It will not be our last.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Hmm, yeah. Let's hope. Anyway, you're right. The river is best. We'll have more attention there. Provided we get off the ground.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: This is the right decision. It would be irresponsible to give up before attempting all other possibilities.
She would not give up again. Her words conjure up an old memory—a friend from years ago in the distant past,
of the last time she had shared this path with someone, and how superstition and fear had taken it away from them, just before they reached their dreams.
And their obstacles here are far less significant. The only thing that stands in her partner's way now is his own ego and greed.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Just think back on how much progress we have made.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Alright. We'll stick to the plan. But if we're taking the river, you'll have to fly. I can't swim.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Not a problem.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Great! I'll get the car and call the reporters.

items.speaker: Victor
items.text: Let's hope we get the headline tomorrow.
